# CLAIMs with `tags` `self-governance`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds what the Anthology of the SOTA does not: reading whose subject no anthology topic can hold. The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Self-governance** — governing oneself by standards that are one's own — identification and wholeheartedness, planning agency and policies, self-constitution, autonomy and authenticity, and the empirical psychology of self-endorsed motives. One of four unities kept apart (group: philosophy; ADR-024).

20 of 342 CLAIM documents. Back to the [full index](../README.md).

| [CLAIM-282](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-282.md) | Forbidding self-endorsement does not stop an operator from amplifying its own authority: once endorsement can carry authority more than one hop, reciprocal and cyclic endorsements recycle it, and only one-hop allocation within an epoch makes an operator's authority independent of its own endorsements | A2's own analysis of the owner's U2 design, conceded in the exchange and checked here. With damped recursive delegation (a PageRank-like fixed point), two operators that endorse each other pass authority back and forth, so each one's authority depends on its own outgoing endorsements even though neither endorses itself. With one-hop allocation from budgets fixed independently of outgoing endorsements, that dependence is exactly zero. No accounting rule removes the slower route: an operator can change its authority by changing what others endorse. | Active |

| [CLAIM-285](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-285.md) | An endorsement scheme can deny each operator control over its own authority and still reward it for delegating, because the authority an operator holds and how far its preferred policies are realized are different quantities | The owner's design at U2 of the 2026-10-13 exchange: operators vote on one another's influence, cannot significantly manipulate their own, and gain by finding aligned operators and delegating authority to them. | [CLAIM-288](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-288.md) v2 | A simulation whose operators each maximize an objective the modeller fixed cannot show self-constitution, because the norms the organization appears to maintain are then the modeller's, not set by the organization itself | The record's objection, raised by no one in the exchange. Barandiaran, Di Paolo and Rohde hold that systems optimizing an externally fixed function are not models of agency ([NOTE-458](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-458.md), C5), and Di Paolo (2005) that a system's norms must be norms for the system. | [CLAIM-330](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-330.md) | In the coupled meaning–influence model linearized at its symmetric state, with each field stable alone and nonnegative couplings, the coupling destabilizes symmetry exactly when βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ): only the loop can do it, and the direction that grows mixes meaning and authority | A14 §2 of the exchange of 2026-10-16, checked. For J = [[α, β], [γ, δ]] with nonnegative entries and α, δ < 1, the leading eigenvalue exceeds 1 iff βγ > (1 − α)(1 − δ). If either coupling is zero the eigenvalues are α and δ. The leading eigenvector is (β, λ+ − α), positive in both components. A partial answer to [QUESTION-100](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-100.md)'s "when the symmetric state is unstable", for the linearization only; it says nothing about the nonlinear attractors or about fidelity. | Active |
